title: P1 Core Network Outage — Mumbai Metro Circle
description: Complete loss of data and voice services for approximately 380,000 subscribers in the Mumbai Metropolitan Area. Enterprise SLA customers on Circle-MH-01 experienced full service blackout. Affected services included 4G LTE, VoLTE, and enterprise MPLS circuits. Incident escalated to P1 after NOC confirmed city-wide scope at 02:31 IST.
initial_suspected_cause: Suspected BGP route flap on upstream peering link caused by a misconfigured ECMP policy applied during a scheduled maintenance window at the BKC PoP.
confirmed_cause: Root cause confirmed as a silent firmware defect in Juniper MX480 (firmware 21.4R3-S2) causing MPLS label stack corruption under traffic loads exceeding 18 Gbps.
cause_revision_note: BGP hypothesis ruled out: packet captures showed no route withdrawals before the outage. Juniper TAC confirmed the firmware defect 8 days post-incident. Initial ECMP theory caused 3 hours of incorrect remediation, delaying restoration ~90 min.

title: P2 Repeat Outage — Mumbai Metro Circle (Partial Service Degradation)
description: Partial service degradation affecting 95,000 subscribers in Andheri, Borivali, and Thane clusters. VoLTE services fully impacted; 4G data degraded to sub-1 Mbps. Incident confirmed as a recurrence of INC-0001 after NOC identified identical MPLS label stack corruption patterns on the same Juniper firmware version. ECMP rollback from the earlier corrective action had no effect.
initial_suspected_cause: Suspected recurrence of MPLS label stack corruption from Juniper firmware defect — ECMP rollback action confirmed insufficient to address underlying defect.
confirmed_cause: Confirmed Juniper MX480 firmware defect (21.4R3-S2) identical to P1 outage. Emergency firmware upgrade to 21.4R3-S4 applied during resolution window.

title: P2 Performance Degradation — Enterprise MPLS Circuits Nationwide
description: High packet loss and latency spikes affecting enterprise MPLS circuits across 14 circles. SLA breach confirmed for 47 enterprise customers. NOC activated Major Incident process. The degradation was traced to a capacity breach on the core optical transport layer following unplanned traffic growth driven by a new IoT platform deployment.
initial_suspected_cause: Suspected DDoS traffic flood on enterprise peering interface causing backpressure on the optical transport layer.
confirmed_cause: Capacity breach on Bengaluru-Mumbai optical transport confirmed. IoT platform traffic grew 340% beyond capacity model projections. Emergency capacity upgrade restored service.
cause_revision_note: Initial DDoS hypothesis ruled out by traffic scrubbing analysis. Optical transport utilisation telemetry confirmed sustained congestion on Bengaluru-Mumbai 100G segment for 4 hours before incident was declared.
